utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I am going to ask the registrar to announce the case, since we had in fact terminated the evidential part of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-98-29/1-T, The Prosecutor versus Dragomir Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I will bypass appearances because we know who we are, by and large. Mr. Tapuskovic, you have nothing?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Microphone, no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can not hear the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear you. Please repeat what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But he can't hear you either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh. Yes, all right. Everything seems to be in order now. Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit, and the procedure that we'll adopt is that the Prosecutor will begin asking questions of the witness. So Mr. Hawking Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. John Docherty for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Good morning, sir, would you begin by introducing yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I'm Wing Commander Andy Knowles currently serving with the Royal Air Force, UK Royal Air Force, and I presume my reason for being here today is that in 1995 I was serving as an UNMO in Sarajevo as a deputy operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And you were indeed summoned for that reason, Wing Commander. Just a couple of housekeeping matters before we begin. All the people in the courtroom that you see around you speak different languages and that's the reason for the head phones. In order that the interpreters' job, which is already very difficult, is not made even more difficult. It is important that you and I not speak over each other and so it's important that you wait until I finish my question, even though you'll often know what the last few words are going to be, and I will observe the same with you. There is a screen in front of you on which the transcript is scrolling continually, and during this trial we found that a good technique for keeping people from talking over each other is wait until the transcript talks before you begin your answer. You and I, Wing Commander, have not met before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And my name, as I said, is John Docherty. I'm one of the attorneys on the Prosecution staff on this case. I understand that you have had some e-mail contact with an investigator for the Office of the Prosecutor named Barry Hogan. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Other than that, have you had any contact with the Office of the Prosecutor in this case?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: To begin, you were together with your summons I believe given some documents, am I correct about that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you should have received a copy of a report by a Captain Hansen, did you get that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you get the report that you wrote in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And did you also get copies of your e-mail correspondence with investigator Hogan?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: With those preliminaries out of the way, could you just tell us, sir, when it was that you were serving as an UNMO in Sarajevo as precisely as you can. If you don't know the day, then the month and the year.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I was serving in Sarajevo, if I can go back, I did a six-month tour in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I initially served out in one of the eastern enclaves in Zepa. I then came back into Sarajevo for the latter part of my six-month tour, so it would have been something like May, June, July of 1995. I was working as operations officer in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you were about three months in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And as an operations officer, you would have been working in the PTT building. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Primarily in the PTT as the deputy operations officer working with Captain Thomas Hansen who was the primary operations officer, but of course our work involved getting out on the ground, going to incidents as well, but primarily inside the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Inside the ops centre in the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And also in the PTT building there were liaison officers from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you are aware, because you have seen the document, that on 4th of July, 1995 you wrote a report concerning an interaction that you had had with some of those liaison officers. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if we could please see Exhibit P519 at e-court page 6 at this time. Do you see on the screen in front of you now, Mr. Knowles, a document?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And is this a correct copy of the report that you wrote on July the 4th of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Now before coming to court today did you have a chance to take a look at this and get reacquainted with it?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And given that 12 years have passed since this was written I imagine it was helpful to you to have a look at it?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, very much so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Because obviously sometimes we can't remember what we did 12 days ago, much less 12 years. Could I please direct you, this says that in the first paragraph that at approximately 1730 hours on 28 June of 1995, you visited the BiH LO's office and 1730, that would be 5.30 in the afternoon in the civilian time, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I will have to accept the daytime group on that report that was written at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. But my question was simply that 1730 in military time translates to 5.30 p.m. for us civilians?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes. We would have been using local time then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And 28 June is the day on which the TV tower was hit or there was an explosion at the TV tower. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the TV tower had been hit some hours earlier, about 9.20 or 9.30 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The incident took place in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. In paragraph 2 it indicates that the liaison officers are upset because of an earlier discussion they'd had with Captain Hansen. And I'm just going to read from paragraph 2: "It was alleged that Captain Hansen had accused the ABiH of firing on their own people with an attack against the TV building." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you react to that in paragraph 3, and again I'll just read and ask you if I've read it properly. "Although I was not aware of the facts, I suggested that I was sure that there had been some misunderstanding most likely due to language difficulties." That's what you wrote on 4 July 1995, correct, Wing Commander?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And then the last thing that I want to draw your attention on this page is in paragraph 5, where you say that your meeting with these liaison officers, which sounds like it got quite contentious, lasted about 40 minutes. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could we please go to e-court page 4 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now on the screen in front of you, Wing Commander, is another report. This one was written by Captain Hansen. His signature block appears on the next page. I don't think this was in the packet that you received with your summons. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That's correct, I have not seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to draw your attention to a couple of things on this document but if you need some time since you haven't seen it before, just say so. It looks first of all as though after you left and duly informed Captain Hansen that Captain Hansen himself went straight to see the liaison officers, and the reason I say that is in the bottom paragraph on this page it says, "At 1800 hours I went to the liaison office." Now if you went in at 5.25.30 and your meeting lasted 40 minutes, then it would seem that Captain Hansen went straight in after you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: It would appear so, but I don't recall Captain Hansen going straight down after my discussion with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I understand. And I understand all the way through this is -- we're talking about things that happened 12 years ago and therefore may have to rely more than usual on the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If we could please go to the next page, e-court page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And here, talking about this row with the BiH liaison officers Captain Hansen says, beginning at the first line, "I believe that the situation started because of language misunderstandings and especially because I was not allowed to finish my conversation." So he has the same diagnosis as you, correct, that there has been a misunderstanding over allegations that he is accusing the Bosnian army of firing upon their own civilians. Is that what the document says?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, that is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: If I can refer you back to my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Certainly. Could we go to page 6, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: When I say in paragraph 3, although I was not aware of the facts, that is referring to I had not been at the earlier meeting with Captain Hansen, so I don't know exactly what had been said apart from the fact Thomas Hansen relayed to me that there had been this explosive situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I understand now and we'll come back to that in a couple of minutes because there is a couple of things about the first meeting with Captain Hansen. But for now let's go back to e-court page 4, which is the first page of Captain Hansen's report. Because I want to just talk for a minute about when Captain Hansen says due to language based on misunderstandings, I want to see if what Captain Hansen is saying is due to language-based misunderstandings. I want to refer you, sir, to the third paragraph from the bottom. It begins: "When I came back from the investigation." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And at the -- I'll just trade in the entirety. "When I came back from the investigation, I was informed that the BiH LO wanted to make an official protest against me because of words he believed that I had said (he stated that I accused the BH army of having killed their own people)." And then this is the sentence that I wanted to pay particular attention to: "I did not use words that could indicate this, but it is it difficult to have a conversation with people when you are prevented from finishing what you want to say." The way I read this is that Captain Hansen is saying that he did not use words that would indicate that he had accused the BH army of firing on its own people. Do you read it the same way or differently?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I was not present at that particular translation, at that meeting and therefore I wouldn't wish to put a subjective interpretation on what Thomas Hansen meant to say or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right, that's fair enough. And lastly if we could, before leaving this exhibit, go to e-court page 1. And while that is coming up let me ask you, do you remember a Lieutenant-Colonel Alam, I believe from Bangladesh who was also with the UN in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I think -- we had a sector commander. I think Lieutenant-Colonel Alam was probably the deputy sector commander at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And are you aware that Lieutenant-Colonel Alam attended a meeting on 29th June with Bosnian army representatives to try and work this situation out?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I was aware there were ongoing discussions to resolve the situation Captain Hansen had found himself in, being declared persona non grata, but I wasn't present at that meeting and wasn't aware of the detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Had he in fact been declared persona non grata, Captain Hansen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The meeting I attended on the afternoon of the incident when the BiH LO got very excited with me as well was when I was told he would be declared persona non grata and would have to leave the country. That is my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you know whether that was actually done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand. I never saw any kind of official document that was signed off with Thomas being declared persona non grata no, although obviously within a number of days Thomas had left that part of the mission, I can only assume as a result of those difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: This, wing commander, I'll just represent to you, it's an exhibit, it is in evidence in this case already through an earlier witness and this is Lieutenant-Colonel Alam's report of his meeting on the 29th of June. And if you ever want to see the signature block or what have you, we can go to those pages. But we have limited time and that's why I'm trying to move along. If you look at paragraph 1-B, Lieutenant-Colonel Alam is here saying, "The LO seemed to have fully misunderstood Captain Hansen altogether. As if Captain Hansen was suggesting that ABiH was firing against their own people." Have you read that accurately?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: You have read the paragraph accurately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So here again Captain Alam in a report that is dated 5 July 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Is still characterizing this allegation that Captain Hansen said that the BH army was firing on his own people as a misunderstanding, correct? That is at least Lieutenant-Colonel Alam's characterisation on 5th July?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: One has to remember this is a very sensitive and difficult situation face-to-face dealing with the liaison officers of the BiH, the point being that the words chosen might not have been very careful and in a very sensitive situation but of course referring to what was reported as the incident. How one wishes to interpreter that is a sensitive issue when dealing face-to-face with very angry people in a war situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. I can understand that. We're going to move away now from the reports and so forth of 28th and 29th June and get into the e-mails. But before we leave these documents, we have seen just to sum up, Captain Hansen and yourself and Lieutenant-Colonel Alam all say that this was a misunderstanding and I take your point about being diplomatic but everyone has said that this was a misunderstanding. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, I don't believe that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Can I continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: If I refer to what I said earlier in my report I think it was paragraph 3, I suggested when I spoke to the LO and said there had probably been a misunderstanding about the facts, that was because I was not at the early meeting that became so aggressive with Captain Hansen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: And therefore my -- my use of the term "misunderstanding" is completely different to what you are suggesting with these two. Either way, Captain Hansen in my report refer to the incidents when I was with Captain Hansen that morning and obviously we have to look that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And that's what we're going to look at now. And we will begin with your e-mail to Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if we could please have 65 ter number 03511 displayed on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And that's -- can you read that? I can't.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, just.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just -- just a minute, please. This is the witness's e-mail --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Of 10 September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- beginning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, it is occurring to me that in the interest of getting everything in sequence, it would be better to begin with your showing the witness Mr. Hogan's e-mail to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, okay. I'm not sure that that has been loaded in e-court. I sent the document list in, but we'll maybe have to take a break and do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me just check with the court registrar. This is the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Docherty. The e-mail that I'm referring to, we'll get at that after you have discussed this one with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Now, what this e-mail says, Mr. Knowles, is that you and Captain Hansen were walking across the PTT building car park morning of 28th June of 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And it says that you heard but does not say that you saw a projectile, at least at first. Later you saw it, but at first it was noise only. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: We heard what we thought was the outgoing report, the launch of some sort of projectile, but of course at that time, having not turned our eyes to catch its trojectory, in Sarajevo there were many outgoing and incoming reports all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And in fact on this particular morning are you aware that a battle for western Sarajevo had begun with a BH army offensive against SRK positions?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes. There was activity on the confrontation lines a lot of the time. I think at that period there was more than usual turned into the launch an offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So there was probably a fair amount of both outgoing and incoming fire at that particular time.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That would be fair to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. After hearing this noise you and Captain Hansen you say then saw a projectile going across and it struck the TV building and there was a tremendous explosion. I'm summarising but is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes. We observed together. As you say, we heard the launch report. We then caught sight of a low flat almost direct-fire type trajectory, slow moving that flew straight across to a front horizontally and impacted the TV building and a couple of buildings up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: When you heard a launch report, is that a military term and if it is, could you just tell us what it -- describe what a launch report is?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Every weapon will have a launch signature an acoustic signature whether it's an artillery piece, a tank in direct fire, a mortar, even a small arms rifle. Everything has a different type of report, and after a fair bit of time in these environments you begin to learn, you know instinctively what is artillery, what is mortars, what is tanks, et cetera. In this case we heard a report type event but from what we saw of the projectile, it was not a conventional type weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What you saw of the projectile. And you nod your head affirmatively there. But the launch report that you heard, before the 28th of June, how many times had you heard a modified air bomb being launched?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I don't recall I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You don't recall that you did?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: My apologies. I don't recall ever hearing the launch of a modified air bomb-type weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. And so what you heard that morning you say you heard a launch report and then saw the projectile?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: An explosive type event which we took to be a launch report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. You then, according to the e-mail, you and Captain Hansen, thinking that this had come from inside the confrontation lines, immediately went and told this to the Bosnian army's liaison officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Not entirely. This is where the 12-year factor kicks in. Can I just expand --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: -- to clarify. When I sent that e-mail to Mr. Barry Hogan, of course that was completely cold, 12 years on, having not seen any other documentation. I obviously recalled visiting the BiH LO myself and getting into an aggressive situation with arms flailing, very excited. In my mind, 12 years on, I assume Thomas and I must have gone together and I must have witnessed that event but, of course, reading these reports when they are sent to me, it is clear to me that Thomas Hansen went to that early meeting on his own. I believe I probably went back into the operations room of our sector headquarters, and then it was later in the day that I went down to see the LOs myself and I of course got subjected to the same type of aggressive response, and I think because I knew that Thomas Hansen had had the similar experience earlier, in my mind 12 years on, I probably thought it was the same event, but it is not. It is two separate meetings. So I think my e-mail to Barry Hogan is slightly incorrect. I did not go with Thomas. I went later in the afternoon. Does that clarify?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Best I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes, I think that is it clear. And are you aware that Captain Hansen gave testimony earlier in this trial?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, I was not until I received the court summons papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. And I know that you have seen his later report but have you seen or heard anything about his testimony?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, not at all. I thought I was doing a service by informing Barry Hogan of the presence of a man called Captain Hansen, thinking he hadn't been spoken to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: No. He -- I appreciate your good motives, but he'd been here. I just want to read to you a portion of the transcript of his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, this is transcript pages 4334, continuing to page 4335, and it concerns the events of 28th June.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: When the bomb -- question: "When the bomb hit were you in the TV building or the PTT building?" Answer: "PTT building." Question - this is from the Prosecutor, not me but one of my colleagues. Question: "Okay. Thank you. After it hit, another UNMO came into the PTT building and spoke with you about what he saw. Is that right?" Answer from Captain Hansen: "He came to make a report about what he had observed. Question: "You yourself did not see anything. Is that right?" Answer: "That's correct." And I mean you can see why I go to that bit of the transcript because you have just told us that Captain Hansen was on the PTT building car park with you and that you and he together saw -- heard the report and saw this projectile flying, but Captain Hansen is saying he was sitting in his office at the PTT building when someone came to see him. I realise you just heard this, but is there any light that you can shed on what appears to be differing recollections?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, not at all. You completely surprised me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: My recollection was that I was with Thomas Hansen. We observed what we observed. He then went down to speak to the LO, leading to that incident that we all know about. I would have gone back to the PTT building and later on that day I went down to see the LO myself. And indeed it was Captain Hansen that then wrote the UN report later that day and submitted it using third person terminology, referring to an UNMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Which I assume that he wrote in the third person so as not to identify himself as the source.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: So I'm afraid my recollection is 180 out there with you. To this day I believe Thomas Hansen and I observed that together and indeed thereafter even went to look at the map to work out where we thought the launch point was to follow-up action. So to hear you say today that Thomas Hansen did not see this is just not my recollection. I'm sorry. I can't add to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Completely surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. I didn't mean to ambush you, but there is a lot of documents and I don't think you've seen them all.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Speaking of, just because you mentioned follow-up action, you indicate in your e-mail that a patrol was sent out, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I think our intention was to task a patrol to go to the area we thought was the launch point to look for any kind of launch debris, any kind of signatures. But again I don't recall 12 years on -- well, I certainly know that nothing was found, but I don't recall seeing a report that was written by that patrol or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But in any event the results were negative?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct. Nothing was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President, could I please tender the e-mail 65 ter number 03511.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P940, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The last thing I just want to draw your attention to one thing on this e-mail and then we'll move along. You indicate in paragraph 1, 2, 3, 4, that you saw a smoke -- launch signature (smoke). Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And I just want to -- you also mentioned Captain Hansen's report that he submitted to UN channels, the one that he wrote in the third person and I'd like to turn to that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So could we please see Exhibit D103.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for that to come up, wing commander, I'm going to begin with that. There is some language in there about smoke and that's where I want to start and then we'll move on to some other topics. On the screen in front of you, this document is also in evidence at this time. It is Exhibit D103. And the format, it's a report by Captain Hansen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: It is released by Lieutenant-Colonel Alam whom we have heard of a few moments ago. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And its subject is special impact on TV building 28/0920 B June 1995 which again to translate the times means 9.20 in the morning, Bosnian time on 28 June of 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And then the format is there's two sort of topic sentences, I'll call them and underneath each there are a number of indented sentences each preceded by a dash; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Let's look at the first topic, the first group, if you will. Talks about an UNMO coming into the PTT building, parking his car on the lower parking place and observed various things and as I said, the fourth from the bottom says there was no smoke observed whilst the low trajectory object was in flight. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you have had a chance to look at this before coming to court, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now are you not the UNMO referred to in this first batch of indented sentences, are you?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Well, again, 12 years on, and I was slightly surprised when I read this because I cannot clarify in my own mind whether this referred to Thomas Hansen's own observations or both of ours combined because I still believe we saw this together, or it may be, therefore, that he is trying to quote me. I'm still surprised by this 180 out with Captain Hansen suggesting he was in the building, and I can't reconcile it in my mind. I taught we were together in that car park 12 years on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In any event, this UNMO says that he saw -- or saw no smoke at any event, whichever one it is, in the first group of indented/dashed sentences?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: The smoke -- there was no smoke behind the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: It was a projectile that appeared to having been launched, then just flew on its trajectory but did not have any kind of rocket motor. There was no smoke signature behind the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Behind the projectile. Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Any smoke or dust being referred to here, from my recollection, was a ground point which one would believe was the launch point unless it was a coincidence at that spot with something else happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Right. And as you mentioned, in terms of coincidences there was a fair amount of both -- of outgoing and incoming fire that day due to the Bosnian army offensive that had just got under way?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Not necessarily due to the offensive that had just gotten under way, that there was regular activity in the mornings. But I take your point, yes, either way, simultaneous activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. When Captain Hansen testified, he testified that the individual in the first batch of indented sentences, the UNMO who was parking his car, was a Muslim UNMO. So that would not be you, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But the second batch of indented sentences - and it continues to the next page - says that this other UNMO heard but did not see. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That's what it says in the text, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And that would not be correct if it were a reference to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, sir, yes, that's what I was interfering. I don't believe that was referring to me at all. My recollection is when I read this report was that everything contained in the upper half of that page refers to what Captain Hansen and I had observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to try and sum things up to this point because then I'm going to turn to external extrinsic evidence not based on you and Captain Hansen. But at this point, understanding it's been 12 years, but in your e-mail to Mr. Hogan you recollected wrongly when you said that you and Hansen went together to see the liaison officer. You heard a launch report on the morning of the 28th, you saw something, it hit the TV building, there was an explosion. A patrol was sent out, it found nothing, and later that day, you had a -- in your word an aggressive interaction with the liaison officer who said Captain Hansen had accused them of shooting their own people. You said that there must be a misunderstanding. Have I fairly summarized what we've talked about so far this morning?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes. Although if I could just clarify, yes, I said there was a misunderstanding. That is because I was not at the early meeting with Captain Hansen. That is not to say that the -- the event did not take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: No, no, no. I mean, we've gone over that.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Otherwise, yes, absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now there was another UNMO that day. Did you during the three months that you spent in Sarajevo ever meet a Norwegian officer named Anton Brennskag? He worked on the Pofalici team.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I'm sure I did, but I'm afraid I can't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you recall where OP 4 was?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Do you have a map at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I have a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If we could please see Exhibit 518.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Docherty, I would like to put a question to the witness about this document before we move on to the following document. It is document D103. Is that it? Yes, Mr. Registrar, I would like you to show the previous document, D103. Witness, there's something I would like to clarify with respect to this document. Let me read out the paragraph and then I will put a question to you. It's the second point heard -- [In English] outgoing projectile across the parking place and road from g-r-i-d and the number, the place is on BiH territory approximately 1800 metres from the [indiscernible], et cetera. [Interpretation] My question is as follows: This grid BP 866587, that is the location where the UNMO officer was or is it the location where he believes the projectile was fired from, grid BP 866587? Which one of the two is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I was confused by that as well when I read the report. I still have my Sarajevo map here with the confrontation lines and all the OPs marked on and the location of the PTT headquarters. That grid reference is the PTT car park where we were observing this -- this projectile. So that is not the launch point. That is the car park where we observed from and it is not clear in that UN report. It's confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is what I was thinking as well. Because we had a high-ranking officer who testified here and made the same comment. That's different, quite different, if this grid reference is not the origin of the projectile but the place where the officer was located. Mr. Prosecutor, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could have Exhibit P518 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What you'll see, wing commander, is a photograph I believe taken from the PTT car park and there will be a red square on it. And I'm going to ask you whether that red square marks the position of the Pofalici team's observation post. Two questions. First, are we looking to the north out of the PTT car -- upper level PTT car park in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. And the red square, does that have any relation to the Pofalici team's OP?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Certainly cross-referring to my map and vaguely from memory, that would be the high point that probably was the OP 4 location, but I can give the grid of the OP 4 location because I've got my map from 1995 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: It wouldn't hurt.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Okay, OP 4 grid reference would be about 864599.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. That's good.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That would correlate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And thanks. Now we've got that in the record. I'm going to play a short video-clip of Mr. Brennskag' testimony when he came here because he testified he was on duty at OP 4 on the morning of 28 June and he talked with the Chamber about what he saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I will ask the case manager to play clip one from Sanction at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The last word got cut off but it was Bosnian Serb army. And if we could now see, Mr. Registrar, Exhibit P347.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And what this is, Wing Commander, is the map that UNMO Brennskag marked as having seen the air bomb launch. Should be coming up on your screen in a moment. This is the map that you just saw Lieutenant-Colonel Brennskag marking on. And you see that circle down in the lower left. According to the launch signature that you heard that morning, could that have been a point from which this device was launched?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Can I explain further?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In one moment. So you disagree with Mr. Brennskag?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Clearly, there is a possibility that there were two projectiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: However, from where we were positioned in the PTT car park, looking northwards watching a projectile trajectory that came from the north-west as we tracked it all the way into the building to impact, anything that would have come from the Ilidza area would have to have overflown our position, would have to have overflown the PTT to strike the TV building slightly further down. So I'm surprised any projectile, unless it was in its terminal ballistic phase dropping down would have struck the PTT building without striking something already in its flight path before. All I can say is whatever that particular UNMO was referring to, that was not the projectile that we observed from the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now you said strike the PTT building. Did you mean to say strike the TV tower?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: The tower, next door.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You also, though, said there was no smoke behind this projectile. And then in this answer you said -- referred to a terminal ballistic phase. Now one of these modified air bombs in its terminal ballistic phase will not be having smoke come out because it's in its terminal ballistic phase because the rocket engines have shot off, that they've run out of fuel. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Well if indeed this modified air bomb had any kind of propulsion system within it, which effectively makes it a rocket, I do not believe it had any kind of rocket inside it. Certainly what we saw did not have a rocket mechanism and therefore creating an eflux and therefore creating a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Now Mr. Brennskag said that this was the projectile that hit the TV tower.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I'll ask the case manager to please play Sanction clip number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: On the morning of the 28th, you just made reference to the possibility of two projectiles. You observed one explosion on the TV tower, however?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you are aware that the Bosnian law enforcement did an investigation of this incident and that the marks on the TV tower were-- on the roof of the TV tower were consistent with a projectile that had been launched from the west but skipped across the roof, if you will, from west to east. Were you aware of that before today?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Were you aware that the structural damage to the TV tower was at the south side of the building, on the south facade of the building?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I did not visit the scene of the TV building myself so I don't know where the damage was, physically cratered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But as a proposition would you agree that it would be difficult for a projectile launched from the north to cause damage at the base of the south side of the building?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: If the impact point, if that's what you're referring to, an impact point, if the impact point was on the southern edge of that building then that projectile had to come from the south, fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Or from the west?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Depending on the angle of impact. Certainly not from the north on the opposite side of the building. That would have been an exit point had it gone right through the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So aerodynamically that would be difficult to achieve. You are a RAF officer so I with use words like "aerodynamic."

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: If the impact point was on the southern side of the building, that projectile did not come from the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware that the United Nations was quite clear that this rocket had been launched by the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, no, I have not seen any kind of follow-up reports or activity from this incident at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, would you like to see a couple? Why don't we start with exhibit P18, please. You're aware that after incidents, if blame can be laid, a protest letter was often sent to a commanding officer on the other side, and you know from your time in Sarajevo who Colonel Robert Meille was of the French army?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: On the screen in front of you is a letter. It is addressed to the accused in this trial, General Dragomir Milosevic. It is from Colonel Meille and it says: "On 28 and 29 June 1995 the Bosnian Serb forces of Romanija Corps launched several attacks, et cetera, et cetera, among them 28 June 0930, an extremely powerful rocket bomb was fired at the TV building." The balance of the letter goes on to express negative feelings about this sort of behaviour. So that is one example anyway of the United Nations concluding that this bomb had been launched by the Bosnian Serbs. Are you aware that on three separate occasions officers of the Bosnian Serb army had said that they were responsible for this attack on the TV building?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If we could please see, Mr. Registrar, Exhibit P629, and I'm going to want page e-court 3 in the English, 2 in the French, 3 in the B/C/S. It is all one page. It is 3 in English and B/C/S; it's 2 in French.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: On the screen in front of you on the right hand is the French, on the left-hand side is the English, and the last paragraph that's visible on the English begins with "he acknowledged." Now this is a memorandum, it is from a Captain Gragogne [phoen] of the French army to Colonel Meille. It is about his meeting with a Bosnian Serb Sarajevo-Romanija Corps officer named Captain Prodanovic. It occurred on the 9th of July 1995, and again if would you be more comfortable seeing these things for yourself, we can go to the first page and have a look. I'm going to read out: "He acknowledged that Kramer rockets had been fired on the city of Sarajevo (about a dozen). This was psychological warfare in that upsetting the Bosnian soldiers engaged on the Treskavica front who would be worried about their safety of their families in Sarajevo. He said that the Bosnian authorities tried to conceal the efficiency of these shots by keeping the press on the television building. In fact, two Kramer rockets were launched on the television building, one of them hit it." You had not been aware of this information before this morning?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Could we -- are you aware that Captain Prodanovic is from a specific brigade, or from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, the Ilidza Brigade. ?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if can you remember the circle that Mr. Brennskag drew on the map, that was in the area of Ilidza, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: It was indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Could we see Exhibit P41, e-court page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And what we're going to be looking at here, Wing Commander, is some signals intelligence, if you will. It is a transcript of an intercepted telephone call between two Serbian army officers and one of them refers to something that General Mladic did. And now again on the left-hand side you've got the English. And I'm just -- there's an individual named Prstojevic and about between a third and halfway down he says, "And if he attacks, he levels." Do you -- got it?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: "As I could see on TV, the television's been hit, that's good." Answer: "Of course it's good. Mladic congratulated it all." Prstojevic responds "Mladic congratulated?" To which Veselinovic says "Sure he did, he called this morning." Prstojevic says, "Well, yeah [indiscernible], that's good, it's good, it's good." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just wanted to check something in my documents. Mr. Docherty did not sate that this was a document marked for identification. Therefore, it is not P41, but P41 MFI and this is part of a set of intercepts related to the person mentioned here. And the Defence is strictly opposed to the admission of these documents. When Mr. 14 came here, the Prosecution tried to tender this document, and we objected. The documents were only marked for identification at the time, and today we see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why was it marked for identification only?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was during the testimony of Mr. 14. I was cross-examining the witness, but I wanted to check things beforehand, before taking the floor. The registrar can do so as well. P41 was an intercept. We can find the part of the transcript where this is referred to, but I'm taken completely by surprise by this document, so I don't know exactly what word to use so as not to exaggerate, but this is it going quite a bit far to state that this document is P41, whether -- whereas it is only a document marked for identification. That's one thing. And the second thing is that in the transcript you will find the reasons why the Defence was opposed to the admission of this document without any additional evidence related to these conversations without possibly the testimony of these interlocutors, these people were talking all the time with everyone during the offensive. There are about -- we have about four days of conversation of Mr. Prstojevic throughout the offensive. At the time he was the mayor of the town. That's why we object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I do not understand why this transcript was given an MFI number only.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I was not expecting this from the Prosecutor. Therefore, I did not bring the transcript of the hearing with me. And I have some problem with my computer as well. I was trying to find the document earlier on. I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, I have been given a note of what I said and I am going -- what I said at the time when it was marked for identification, and we'll consult on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, the transcript of the proceedings, or one part of it indicate that one reason, at any rate, for marking the documents for identification was that you not been served with them. I say here: "We'll mark these documents for identification. Counsel will transmit them to you after the hearing. We'll have to investigate independently whether you were in fact served with the documents. If we find that you were not served and you are in any way embarrassed in your preparation for cross-examination, we'll take that into consideration." You have in fact now been served with the documents. Or was there another issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But there was another problem because the report continues, stating that there was a big bulk of such intercepts and we have not received these documents. This is the reason why we objected. And in the meantime, we received the documents, we continued to object to the -- accepting these documents where the witness appears, and we accepted tendering all the intercepts where Mr. Milosevic appears, because in the meantime he said, yes, I accept. And you can look at the list of documents admitted that day, and you will see that there are intercepts that are P documents, not marked for identification, and the conversations where this gentleman appears remain marked for identification, and it was up to the Prosecutor to find the necessary evidence so that we can accept them as real evidence. That was what was mentioned. It is mentioned in the report, and I'm sorry, this is not something that I expected, and with this witness who is not aware of all that, I did not believe that the Prosecution would dare show this document without telling the others that this is a document marked for identification. Because this may have been the judge's focus on what the witness is saying, but we have to be very cautious, but unfortunately these are things that happen. And I believe this is a mistake, just happened by chance, but nevertheless this is something that has to be taken into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're not suggesting that the mere fact that a document has been marked for identification means that it cannot be shown to another witness. What you're objecting to is the fact that the Prosecution misidentified it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. First of all, I object to that; and then maybe if he wanted to tender this document with this witness that, will be another point that I object to. But for the time being, this is what I am objecting to and we have to be very cautious with everything we are doing now, everything we have to do now. We keep checking all the evidence because when you say P41, it should be document P41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: First, several things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: A couple of things, Your Honour. First of all, to clarify, I believe the objection at the end of it all distils to I said P41 rather than P41 marked for identification, and I take the correction but I don't know that there's any substantive difference that that makes. A couple of things on the disclosure issue. Our records which we were checking during the colloquy indicate that these documents were served on the Defence on 21 November of 2006. Over and above that, these were first attempted to be used with Lieutenant-Colonel Fortin of the Canadian army. He was one of the first witnesses in the trial. He testified in January. So the Defence has certainly had notice of them since then. But as I say, I don't see a substantive difference. I made an innocent mistake when I said P41 rather than P41 MFI, but with that correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It remains now to be seen whether Ms. Isailovic has a substantial objection to this document being put to the witness and if so, what is it. It remains -- the status of the document remains a document marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we go across the room can I add one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Which is that yesterday we served the usual spreadsheet of documents that we're going to use with witnesses, as did the Defence, and this document appears on and we sent that over I can't be more precise than late in the afternoon yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, excuse me for taking all the time -- so much time because I know we have a lot of things to do, the Defense have a lot of things to do, and we are preparing something really urgent and there are two of us, and the problem -- the same problem is still valid. It is true that we received or the Prosecution sent us the list late in the afternoon but this is what I have a problem, because not marking this document the way it should be marked because it is a MFI document, I must admit I have not paid any attention to the document and it is only when I saw it now, because I know the document well, and it is true that the Defence does not have much time and we tried to do our best to prepare ourselves properly and with this kind of mistake and all the mistakes that may have taken place, I realise and I understand that this was just a very -- absolutely innocent, but the transcript mentions an objection -- well, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There's a message.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I realise that there was an objection to these intercepts. And these objections were much stronger than communication as I just said. As I'm speaking I cannot check the transcript at the same time. I hope you're hearing exactly what I'm saying. And the objection was much stronger than the lack of communication. So this lack of communication before or concerning the tendering of these documents and my assistant just found out that it was on January the 16th, and she even found the exact pages. The registrar did exactly the same thing. The problem was this -- was this person, as Mr. Milosevic and no other person in this court were present at the time these conversations took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Isailovic. I've located with the help of the registrar other passages from the transcript, and you did in fact advance another objection, another basis for objecting to this document. I see here where I say to Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us go to private session. I'm told we should go to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Knowles, what we have on the screen now is a message from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command, going to the corps and to Trnovo and all SRK units, and it is a report on the situation at the front and deals with the offensive that we've talked about a few times. If we-- we'll look at the second page if we need to, but it is signed by Dragomir Milosevic, who is the defendant in this case. It is a bit difficult to navigate on this because of the lack of indents and paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry, Ms. Isailovic has a point here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One objection, the document has not been signed. You just have the name of Dragomir Milosevic but the document does not bear any signature. Maybe it is a problem with interpretation, but I believe that the same applies to the English text.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a telex and there's been testimony in this trial that telexes typically are not signed. In addition the objection just made is an objection to the admission of the document. Since the document has already been admitted into evidence, I don't think that it has force, in terms of using this document with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have already admitted this document, Ms. Isailovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since I believe I may have been misunderstood I just objected to presenting this document, because Mr. Docherty told that the document, that the document has been sign, was signed. Signed mean that there is a signature, while there is no signature on this document. That was my only objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, again, the objection to a misstatement by Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Wing Commander, down on the -- about halfway down the page, "The Serbian soldiers are displaying unprecedented heroism, not letting the enemy get." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now if you could just go down to the semi-indent, I will call it, is an indent from the right. The very next one. The last sentence before that reads, "In one such response on 28 June they hit the BH radio and television, the centre of media lies against the just struggle of the Serbian people." And I probably should have started a bit earlier. "Our artillery forces are responding with precision to -- "

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would like to have the text in B/C/S and English on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, can the text in B/C/S and English be put on the screen for the benefit of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I don't know the page number in B/C/S. Interpreters indicate we can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: "Our artillery forces are responding with precision to the Muslim artillery attacks. In one such response on 28 June, they hit the BH radio and television centre, the centre of media lies against the just struggle of the Serbian people." Had you been aware before today, Mr. Knowles, that there was a document over the accused's name in which he indicated that it was SRK artillery that had hit the TV tower on the 28th of June?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Wing commander, just a -- I'm almost done. I just want to sum up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And would that knowledge which you now have make you change any of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, if I had been aware of some of the subsequent investigations and the reports released by both United Nations and transcripts from Serbian command, then, clearly, and I accept that if the impact was on the southern side of the building, clearly there are two events here that happened because I did not imagine what I saw in the car park that day and it seems to me that therefore the projectile that we observed was a secondary projectile that clearly, having followed its trajectory, appeared to strike the TV building or indeed from our perspective it might have gone behind it but there was an impact coincident at the time. No one, including me would want to dispute all the facts being presented. I think mine is a secondary event. But I did not imagine that projectile crossing the valley that morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When you say secondary event, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. Clearly, from the ballistic evidence that has been referred to with a some sort of munition striking the southern side of the building, that was obviously not the one that I observed that morning, and therefore I am suggesting because clearly, I not made this up nor did I make up the report we wrote that morning. I'm suggesting there must have been two munitions that we are discussing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And just to be clear, I'm not saying there was an impact on the southern side of the building, I'm saying that there was a -- there were marks on the roof of the building that coincided with the projectile coming from the west and then damage at the base of the southern side of the building.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I see. Slightly more complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Slightly more complex, and I'm not saying that there was an actual impact on the south side. I'm not ruling it out but I'm not saying that there was. And just to be clear, Wing Commander Knowles, I'm not in any way suggesting that you're making things up or that you're imagining things, but it is correct, is it not, that this happened 12 years ago?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That it was a sudden and unexpected event when it did happen?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That it happened quite quickly?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And that as you have said in your testimony earlier, you had not seen a modified air bomb launch?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll take the break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And good morning, witness. My name is Branislava Isailovic. I'm a lawyer with the Paris bar and I'm with Mr. Tapuskovic and our case manager. We are working on behalf of Mr. Dragomir Milosevic accused in this court. I hope that Prosecution explained everything about this before you came into the courtroom. So you please wait -- I don't know if you understand French. But we will proceed slowly, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic just mentioned I hope the Prosecution explained everything about this before you came into the courtroom. Just to be clear, the Prosecution other than the e-mails has had no contact with the witness, since is he a Chamber's witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, this is a court witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree, because I will start with the correspondence with Mr. Barry Hogan. Barry Hogan is the investigator working -- it's a key person in the OTP side, so I don't really agree with Mr. Docherty's objection, but I will immediately show you why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, would you agree with me when you agree with what I'm say -- could you say out loud yes or say no when you don't not agree. You cannot just, you know, shake your head because this will not be written on the transcript, so you have to say something openly. So let's start with that correspondence you had with the OTP. Could we please pull up on the screen the -- 422D, Exhibit 422D on the 65 ter list. It is an e-mail and we will look at it together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I ask that that not be broadcast, Mr. President, because it has internal ICTY e-mail addresses on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can it be redacted on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is that a good enough reason for it not to be broadcast?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm not objecting to the document. It can be used without limits. I'm just asking that that e-mail address not be-- I'm just thinking of things like computer security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the court deputy will take account of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please confirm that on the screen you see the document?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Was this the first e-mail you received from Mr. Barry Hogan?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I think this is the response from Mr. Barry Hogan. This is the second e-mail, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, do you remember the content of the first contact you had with Mr. Hogan and do you remember at what date you had this first contact?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I'm afraid not, the detail. The only correspondence I had was from Mr. Hogan. This incident came completely out of the blue, the fact that there was a court sitting at the moment and that I might be required to give some more information. That is the only correspondence I've had with Mr. Hogan, two or possibly three e-mails, no more. Thereafter it became a verbal -- I was contacted through my Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I had gathered. How many telephone calls have you had with Mr. Hogan?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I have not spoken to Mr. Barry Hogan verbally. My contact with the Tribunal has been with Mrs. Marry Banoci via telephone. I have not spoken to any of the individuals here today.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And you can confirm that the first contact you had was through e-mail. You received an e-mail sort of out of the blue from Mr. Barry Hogan. That's it?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes. And I believe that was the result of, I suspect, Thomas Hansen naming me and I was contacted through the Ministry of Defence in the UK. I think there had been an attempt to track me down.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, did you know Captain Idriz, a Kenyan UNMO, do you remember this person, a Kenyan UNMO named Idriz?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I'm afraid not. With regard to the Norwegian UNMO as well, we all worked together over that period of time. There were UNMOs from many countries there, but 12 years on I don't remember the individual names, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: What about Mr. Brennskag. You don't remember his name either, right?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: That is correct. But having seen him on video I now recognise him and remember who he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We started by looking at a map, and if we could put something on the ELMO. I believe that would the easiest way to proceed but in e-court it is document P517. With your indulgence, can we please have it on the ELMO. Could we please have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, Judge Mindua earlier asked you a question about the grid references. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So I see that as any operations officer you have a map with you, with grid references and we -- we really missed all that in the previous proceedings because we have a lot of reports with these grid references but we're sort of in the dark when it comes to these grid references.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honour, it might be useful to do something so that in the documents we have these maps with grid references in the case file. Otherwise sometimes it is difficult to interpret the UNMO reports without the grid references.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, please, could you look at the map that is on the ELMO, on the screen. On this map we have a grid reference, 866587. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: However, I don't think that this really corresponds to the reference written on your on map. Earlier you said that this -- that this is the grid reference of the PTT building. I have noted the same thing as Judge Mindua. It seemed that the text of the report is quite confusing when it says from grid reference. The way I interpret it was that this was the reference, the grid reference for the PTT building. So could you confirm this for me, that this 866587, according to the map that you have with you, corresponds to the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I do not have the -- the PTT building marked precisely on my map, but looking at it now, 12 years on, I would suggest that this is the location of the PTT building, where we observed the event. I confirmed earlier that OP4 was this location.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So when you look at this map, on this map that we have on the screen, do you believe that this is accurate because the grid reference 866587 is quite far from the PTT building on this map?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I see what you mean now. The PTT is clearly marked. I cannot remember exactly in this area which the PTT building was. That is what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: If that map is correct, then that is the PTT building. I accept that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So in such case, according to you, this map that's on the screen is not correctly identified. If the PTT building represents grid reference 866587, then this exhibit has not been identified properly. Please take a close look and maybe compare with the map that you have with you.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: If that is the PTT building, that is the PTT building, if that is correct, that in the car park adjacent to that is where we would have been standing that morning, so the debate is the accuracy of this and whether that was in the report intending to state what we thought was a launch point or if that is inaccurately transcribed as the PTT building grid.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to finish on this topic, you still maintain that the grid reference 866587 corresponds to something that is south of the river. You probably have the river on your map. But here on this map that we have on the screen, it seems to me east of the river.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're saying. If that is the PTT, then that is the PTT. That is where we were standing that morning in the car park.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that is reference 866587?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
utterances.text: Well, clearly not. If that is 866587, that is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's why I'm asking the question. It doesn't seem to be really accurate. I mean, this map is not cast in stone. It has been marked by another UNMO. It's another UNMO that annotated all this. So please check. You have your own map with you, but could you please tell me whether on the map that's on the screen that has been annotated by another witness in this case, please tell us whether the annotations are accurate or not. You have my question.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW KNOWLES
